The server feels slow, what can I run?

Memory is the bottleneck: agents' test browsers and old demo offices stay around after their sessions. Three things to paste, quickest first. Each one is safe to run while agents work; none of them touches the live office or its state.

## A. Quick wins (a minute)
See what is using memory and swap right now, biggest first:
```bash
free -h
ps -eo pid,rss,etime,cmd --sort=-rss | head -15
swapon --show
```

## B. Old previews and demo offices
List what listens on the agents' preview ports and how long it has been running, so you can stop the leftovers by pid:
```bash
ss -ltnp | grep -E ":(5[0-9]{3}|6[34][0-9]{2})"
pgrep -af "server/index.ts --demo"
```

## C. The disk
Free space and the biggest working copies:
```bash
df -h /
du -sh ~/.cubefarm/machines/* | sort -h | tail
```

## D. If swap stays full
Watch it for a minute: if `si` and `so` stay above zero, the box is swapping and agents will slow down until something is stopped.
```bash
vmstat 5 12
```

experiments.name: Test first vs current
experiments.hypothesis: Writing a failing test before the code gets PRs through QA in fewer rounds, and they survive longer.

settings.prompt: Before changing any code, write a test that fails without your change and run it to see it fail; then make it pass.

experiments.name: Plan in the PR vs none
experiments.hypothesis: A short written plan before coding gives smaller diffs and a higher first-round QA pass.

settings.prompt: Before coding, write a short plan (files to change, approach, risks) and put it at the top of your pull request description.

experiments.name: Self-review skill vs none
experiments.hypothesis: Reviewing the diff with the simplify skill before pushing gets PRs through QA in fewer rounds.

settings.prompt: Before pushing, review your diff with the simplify skill (or code-review at low effort) and fix what it finds.

experiments.name: Cross-model QA vs same model
experiments.hypothesis: Codex testing Claude's PRs catches more: fewer reverts and follow-up bugs. Uses Codex agents already on the floor; never hires one.

experiments.name: Fixes at medium vs high effort
experiments.hypothesis: High effort for fixes costs more per session but fewer rounds, so less per merge.

experiments.name: Up to date before merge vs current
experiments.hypothesis: Merging only PRs brought up to date with main and green on that result means fewer red mains and fewer follow-up fixes.

experiments.name: File leases vs current
experiments.hypothesis: Holding back issues whose files overlap work in flight means fewer conflict fixes and fewer QA rounds.

experiments.name: Auto-rebase vs current
experiments.hypothesis: Updating conflicting PRs as soon as main moves, before QA, gets them merged sooner with fewer QA rounds.

experiments.name: Conflict-aware scheduling vs current
experiments.hypothesis: Starting issues away from busy files and merging the hottest PR first means fewer conflict rounds and fewer QA rounds per merge.

experiments.name: Small-PR budget vs none
experiments.hypothesis: A 400-line soft budget gives smaller diffs, a higher first-round QA pass and better survival.
